answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token as collateral before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers prove fraud. Creating a thousand accounts no longer grants a thousand free votes: every account ties up capital, and dishonest accounts risk losing it. The collateral can be a relic, lotus, or ivory token, provided each has verifiable scarcity and the same enforceable penalty. A patient attacker can still buy influence, but must fund every identity and expose that capital to loss.
